project_meta.title: Complete DevOps Mini Project on Azure

real_world_problem_statement.scenario: Socho ek startup hai jahan 5 developers kaam karte hain. Har baar jab koi code change karta hai, manually server pe jaake code update karna padta hai. Ek developer ne galti se production server pe wrong code deploy kar diya - 2 ghante downtime hua. Boss ne bola - automate karo ye sab!
problems_with_manual_deployment: Human error - galti hone ke chances bahut zyada
Time waste - har deployment mein 30 minutes lagta hai
No consistency - har baar alag tarike se deploy hota hai
No rollback - agar kuch galat hua toh pata nahi kaise fix kare
No audit trail - kisne kya deploy kiya, koi record nahi
real_world_problem_statement.solution: CI/CD Pipeline - Code push karo, baaki sab automatic ho jayega

why_this_project_matters.for_learning: Ye project real companies mein use hone wale tools aur practices sikhata hai. Interview mein jab ye project dikhaaoge, interviewer samjhega ki tum practical DevOps jaante ho.
why_this_project_matters.interview_value: 90% DevOps interviews mein CI/CD aur Docker ke questions aate hain. Ye project dono cover karta hai with real implementation.

what_skills_this_proves: You can set up infrastructure on cloud
You can write and debug CI/CD pipelines
You know how to secure deployments

what_is_ci.simple_explanation: CI ka matlab hai ki jab bhi koi developer code push kare, automated tests aur builds run ho jaayein. Isse pata chal jaata hai ki naya code purane code ke saath work kar raha hai ya nahi.
what_is_ci.analogy: Socho jaise ek building ban rahi hai. Har din shaam ko inspector aata hai check karne ki aaj ka kaam sahi hua ya nahi. Agar galti mili, toh turant pata chal gaya.

what_is_cd.simple_explanation: CD ka matlab hai ki jo code tests pass kar gaya, wo automatically production tak pahunch jaaye. Manual deployment ki zaroorat nahi.

difference.continuous_delivery: Automated testing tak, deployment manual approval ke baad
difference.continuous_deployment: Fully automated - test pass hua toh seedha production mein

what_is_cd.analogy: Jaise factory mein conveyor belt - product bana, quality check hua, automatically packaging mein chala gaya.

reasons: Free hai for public repos (2000 minutes/month private ke liye bhi)
GitHub ke saath integrated hai - alag tool setup nahi karna
YAML based - easy to understand aur version control mein rehta hai
Huge marketplace - pre-built actions available hain
alternatives: Jenkins - self-hosted, more control but more maintenance
GitLab CI - agar GitLab use kar rahe ho
Azure DevOps - Microsoft ecosystem mein ho toh

section_1_name_and_triggers.code:
name: CI/CD Pipeline - Build and Deploy to Azure VM

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

explanation.name: Workflow ka naam - GitHub UI mein dikhega
explanation.on_push: Jab main branch pe push ho, tab trigger ho
explanation.on_pull_request: Jab main pe PR aaye, tab bhi run karo (testing ke liye)
explanation.workflow_dispatch: Manual trigger button enable karta hai GitHub UI mein

section_2_env_variables.code:
env:
  DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME: devops-flask-app
  CONTAINER_NAME: flask-app-container
  APP_PORT: 5000
section_2_env_variables.explanation: Global environment variables - poore workflow mein use ho sakte hain. Ek jagah define, har jagah use.

section_3_build_job.code:
jobs:
  build-and-test:
    name: Build and Test Application
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

explanation.jobs: Workflow mein multiple jobs ho sakte hain - parallel ya sequential
explanation.runs-on: Kaunsa runner use karna hai - GitHub hosted Ubuntu VM free milta hai

section_4_checkout.explanation: Pre-built action jo repository ka code runner pe clone karta hai. Bina iske code available nahi hoga.

section_5_python_setup.code:
- name: Set up Python 3.11
  uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: '3.11'
    cache: 'pip'
section_5_python_setup.explanation: Python install aur configure karta hai. cache: pip dependencies cache karega - next run faster hoga.

section_6_docker_build.code:
- name: Build Docker Image
  run: |
    cd app
    docker build -t ${{ env.DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
    docker build -t ${{ env.DOCKER_IMAGE_NAME }}:latest .

explanation.run: Shell commands directly run karta hai
explanation.github.sha: Current commit ka unique ID - image versioning ke liye
explanation.latest_tag: Ek image ko multiple tags de sakte hain

section_7_deploy_job.code:
deploy:
  needs: build-and-test
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'

explanation.needs: Ye job tab hi chalegi jab build-and-test succeed ho
explanation.if_condition: Sirf main branch pe push hone pe deploy karo, PR pe nahi

script.dialogue: DevOps seekh rahe ho ya sirf tools ke naam ratt rahe ho? Bahut saare log Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins ke naam jaante hain but actually kabhi use nahi kiya. Aaj hum ek complete project karenge - real Azure VM pe, real CI/CD pipeline ke saath, jo tum apne interview mein confidently present kar sako. Ye 'hello world' nahi hai, ye actual deployment workflow hai jo companies mein hota hai. Agar tum ye video end tak dekhte ho, toh tumhare paas ek working project hoga jo GitHub pe dikhega aur interviewer impress hoga. Chalo shuru karte hain.

Pehle samjho kya banana hai. Flow ye hai - local machine pe code likhenge, GitHub pe push karenge, GitHub Actions automatically trigger hoga, wo SSH se Azure VM pe connect karke Docker container deploy kar dega. Simple. Ab isko thoda detailed samjho. Humare paas teen main components hain - Source Code jo GitHub pe rahega, CI/CD Pipeline jo GitHub Actions handle karega, aur Target Server jo Azure VM hai. Jab developer push karta hai, GitHub webhook trigger hota hai, wo Actions ko batata hai ki kaam shuru karo. Actions pehle code ko checkout karta hai, tests run karta hai, Docker image build karta hai, aur agar sab pass ho gaya toh SSH karke Azure VM pe deploy kar deta hai. Ye sab 2-3 minutes mein ho jaata hai bina kisi manual intervention ke.

Azure Portal pe jaate hain. portal.azure.com pe login karo Azure for Students account se. Agar student account nahi hai toh free tier wala bhi use kar sakte ho initially. Virtual Machines pe click karo aur Create. Subscription Azure for Students select karo, Resource Group naya banao - 'devops-project-rg'. VM ka naam dedo 'devops-vm'. Region choose karo - mere case mein Central India. Image mein Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS select karo. 22.04 isliye kyunki ye LTS hai - Long Term Support - matlab 5 saal tak security updates milenge. Production mein hamesha LTS use karo. Size mein Standard_B1s select karo - ye free tier mein aata hai. 1 vCPU aur 1 GB RAM. Learning ke liye enough hai. Authentication type mein SSH public key select karo - password se zyada secure hai. Username dedo 'azureuser'. SSH key generate new select karo. Inbound ports mein SSH, HTTP aur ek custom port 5000 add karo. Review + Create pe click karo. Create hone pe private key download hogi - ye .pem file bahut important hai, isse safe rakho. Agar ye file kho gayi toh VM mein login nahi kar paaoge.

Ab VM se connect karte hain. Terminal kholo. Pehle key file ki permissions fix karo - chmod 400 karke key file pe. Ye isliye kyunki SSH strict hai permissions ke baare mein. Agar key file world readable hai toh SSH refuse kar dega connect karne se. Security feature hai ye. Ab ssh command use karo - ssh -i path/to/key.pem azureuser@YOUR_VM_IP. First time connect karte waqt fingerprint accept karna hoga. Yes type karo. Agar connected ho gaye toh green prompt dikhega with VM name. Tum ab Azure VM pe ho!

Server ko prepare karte hain. Pehle sudo apt update - ye package list refresh karta hai. Phir sudo apt upgrade -y - installed packages update karta hai. -y flag automatic yes ke liye hai. Ab Docker install karo - sudo apt install -y docker.io. Docker.io Ubuntu ka official package hai Docker ke liye. Install hone ke baad sudo systemctl start docker - Docker daemon start karta hai. Daemon ek background service hai jo containers manage karti hai. sudo systemctl enable docker - ye ensure karta hai ki system restart hone pe Docker automatically start ho. Ab important step - sudo usermod -aG docker $USER. Ye tumhare user ko docker group mein add karta hai. Isse sudo ke bina docker commands chal jayenge. Lekin ye change apply hone ke liye logout karke wapas login karna hoga. Git bhi install karo - sudo apt install -y git. Ab verify karo - docker --version aur git --version. Versions dikh rahe hain? Sab sahi hai.

Dockerfile samjho - ye Docker image ki recipe hai. FROM python:3.11-slim - base image set karta hai. Slim version 900MB ki jagah 150MB hai. WORKDIR /app - container ke andar working directory set karta hai. COPY requirements.txt - pehle sirf requirements copy karo. Kyu? Docker layer caching. Agar requirements nahi badle, ye layer cached rahegi. RUN pip install - dependencies install. Phir COPY . . - baaki code copy karo. USER appuser - non-root user se run karo, security ke liye. Root se run karna risky hai. EXPOSE 5000 - documentation hai ki container 5000 pe listen karega. HEALTHCHECK - Docker automatically check karega container healthy hai ya nahi. CMD - final command jo container start hone pe chalega. Gunicorn use kar rahe hain kyunki Flask ka built-in server production ke liye nahi hai. Gunicorn proper worker management karta hai.

GitHub Actions workflow samjho. .github/workflows folder mein YAML file hoti hai. on: section define karta hai kab workflow trigger ho. push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch - teen triggers hain. jobs: section mein actual kaam define hota hai. Humara pehla job build-and-test hai. runs-on: ubuntu-latest matlab GitHub ka hosted runner use hoga - free hai. Steps mein actions/checkout code laata hai, setup-python Python install karta hai, phir hum dependencies install karte hain, lint karte hain, Docker image build karte hain. Doosra job deploy hai. needs: build-and-test matlab pehle build succeed ho toh hi deploy chalega. if condition check karti hai ki main branch pe push hua hai - PR pe deploy nahi chahiye. appleboy/ssh-action SSH connection handle karta hai. secrets.AZURE_VM_HOST, secrets.AZURE_VM_SSH_KEY - ye values GitHub Secrets se aati hain, encrypted hain. SSH ke andar jo script hai wo VM pe run hoti hai - git pull, docker build, docker run.

GitHub Secrets setup karte hain. Repository Settings mein jaao. Secrets and variables > Actions. New repository secret. AZURE_VM_HOST - apni VM ka public IP daalo. AZURE_VM_USERNAME - azureuser. AZURE_VM_SSH_KEY - ye important hai. Local machine pe cat command se .pem file ka content dekho aur poora copy karo - BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY se lekar END RSA PRIVATE KEY tak sab. Ye encrypted store hota hai. Tum bhi retrieve nahi kar sakte baad mein, sirf update ya delete kar sakte ho. Logs mein ye values *** dikhti hain.

Final testing. Pehle locally check karo - cd app, docker build -t devops-flask-app ., docker run -d -p 5000:5000 --name test-app devops-flask-app. Browser mein localhost:5000 kholo - app dikh raha hai? /health endpoint check karo. Sab kaam kar raha hai. Container stop aur remove karo. Ab git add ., git commit -m 'Initial commit', git push origin main. GitHub pe jaao - Actions tab mein workflow running dikhega. Pehle build-and-test job chalegi, green tick aaya matlab pass. Phir deploy job chalegi. 2-3 minutes mein complete ho jayega. Ab browser mein YOUR_VM_IP:5000 kholo. Congratulations! Tumhara application Azure VM pe deployed hai, automatically, bina manually SSH kiye!

Kuch common mistakes aur debugging tips. Agar SSH fail ho raha hai - VM running hai? NSG mein port 22 allow hai? IP address sahi hai? Key file ka path sahi hai? Permission denied - key file permissions check karo, 400 honi chahiye. Docker permission denied - logout karke wapas login karo, usermod ke baad ye zaroori hai. Application accessible nahi - Azure NSG mein port 5000 allow hai? Container running hai docker ps se check karo. Container crash ho raha - docker logs container-name se logs dekho, error message padho. Health check fail - application start hone mein time lagta hai, wait karo. YAML syntax error - online YAML validator use karo, indentation matter karta hai YAML mein.

Interview mein kaise explain karo? Interviewer poochega - 'Tell me about your DevOps project.' Ye bolo - 'I built a complete CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions that automatically deploys a containerized Flask application to an Azure VM. When I push code to the main branch, the pipeline runs tests, builds a Docker image, and deploys via SSH. I used GitHub Secrets for secure credential management and implemented health checks for deployment verification.' Agar deep dive poochein - architecture explain karo, Docker layers batao, Gunicorn vs Flask dev server difference batao, SSH key authentication explain karo. Important hai ki tum ye project khud se kiya ho - interviewer detect kar lete hain agar copy-paste kiya hai.

Ye project basic hai but foundation strong hai. Aage kya seekh sakte ho? Kubernetes for orchestration, Terraform for infrastructure as code, monitoring with Prometheus, multi-environment deployments. Ye project tumhare GitHub profile pe rahega - recruiters dekhte hain. Agar video helpful lagi toh like karo, subscribe karo, aur comment mein batao kaunsa topic next cover karu. Koi doubt ho toh pooch sakte ho. Happy learning!
